first_impression.reaction: Chloe sent it, so I read it properly. The opening is plain English and tells me what I'm getting: 'Each style gets a plain description, a "suits you if" line and a "think twice if" line'. Sensible. It's a ring article though, not really my department. I'm paying towards the wedding, not the ring.

journey.quote: Fly with the ring in your carry-on, tell your insurer your travel dates and confirm the policy covers loss and damage as well as theft.
journey.reaction: Good. That's exactly what I'd tell her myself. Someone here thinks about insurance, which is more than most of these sites.

journey.quote: GIA separates the setting (how a gemstone is secured, such as claws or a bezel) from the setting style (the overall arrangement of stones, such as solitaire, halo or three-stone), and the same setting can produce very different looks.
journey.reaction: Quoting the gem institute rather than just opinions reassures me. I'd forward this bit to Peter.

journey.quote: Many small stones mean more maintenance, and GIA notes halo claws tend to wear faster, so routine jeweller checks matter.
journey.reaction: Practical and honest. It doesn't pretend the sparkly option is free of cost or bother.

journey.quote: Suits you if: the wearer is an understated contrarian who likes a familiar shape seen differently.
journey.reaction: 'Understated contrarian'? I had to read that twice. A bit too clever for me, but it's a passing line.

journey.quote: full eternity bands are generally treated as not resizable.
journey.reaction: Useful to know before anyone spends money on one. This is the kind of thing nobody tells you until it's too late.

journey.section: From the ring to the wedding abroad
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as one point of contact from first idea to the last dance.
journey.reaction: One point of contact is what I want. But 'payments' makes me sit up: who holds the deposits, and are they protected? It doesn't say, and there's no name or phone number.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor will take it from there, in your time zone and quoting in AUD.
journey.reaction: Quoting in AUD and in our time zone is exactly right. I'd still want to speak to a real person on the phone before anything happens.

unanswered_questions: When the Advisor handles 'payments', are the deposits held in trust or protected if an overseas supplier folds?
Can I ring someone, and who exactly? Is there a named person or a phone number?
Are your fees agreed in writing before anything is booked?
Does your travel insurance advice extend to the guests, particularly older relatives with medical needs?

turn_offs_found.quote: Suits you if: the wearer is an understated contrarian who likes a familiar shape seen differently.
turn_offs_found.why: Reads like a fashion magazine. A small thing, not slang, but it's not how I talk.

would_share_with: My husband (the insurance and resizing bits)
My daughter, back to her, with the eternity band warning circled

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, talk to Wedded Concierge about a wedding abroad.
cta_reaction.why: Not from a ring article on its own. If Chloe's serious about overseas I'd click, but I'd want a phone number and some word on how deposits are handled before I fill in any form.

top_3_changes: Where it says the Advisor handles 'payments', add one line on how deposits and supplier contracts are handled and who is accountable, even if that's just a link.
Give the closing section a person and a phone call: say an Advisor will ring you before anything is booked.
Swap 'understated contrarian' for plainer words, e.g. 'someone who likes a classic shape with a twist'.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes the draft exactly
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, plain-spoken, practical)
No invented brand facts; missing details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments and fact markers treated as invisible

assumptions: The daughter's name (Chloe) and husband's name (Peter) are in-character colour only and not brand facts.
Margaret is not funding the ring, so relevance is naturally low for this topic.
